reason.cpu: CPU is close to full at peak.

advice.growNone: A bigger size at your provider would help.

advice.hubBox: This is the machine Tugra runs on. Resize it from your provider's panel.

guide.title: Resize {name} at {provider}

hetzner.s1: Open Hetzner Console, pick the project and open {name}.
hetzner.s2: Power it off from the Power tab (a graceful shutdown).
hetzner.s3: Open Rescale and choose {plan}. Pick “CPU and RAM only” so the disk stays and you can go back.
hetzner.s4: Rescale, then power it on. Tugra reconnects by itself.

digitalocean.s1: Open the DigitalOcean control panel and open the droplet {name}.
digitalocean.s2: Power it off from the Power tab.
digitalocean.s3: Open Resize, choose {plan} and pick “CPU and RAM only” so the disk stays.
digitalocean.s4: Resize, then power it on. Tugra reconnects by itself.

vultr.s1: Open the Vultr customer portal and open {name}.
vultr.s2: Stop the server from the Settings page.
vultr.s3: Open Change Plan and choose {plan}. Keep the current disk size.
vultr.s4: Apply, then start it. Tugra reconnects by itself.

generic.s1: Open your provider's panel and find {name}.
generic.s2: Shut the server down from there.
generic.s3: Change its size to {plan}. Keep the current disk size, disks cannot shrink.
generic.s4: Power it on. Tugra reconnects by itself.

guide.downtime: Expect a few minutes of downtime.

rescale.title: Resize {name} to {plan}?
rescale.body: The server shuts down, changes size and starts again. Expect a few minutes of downtime. The disk keeps its size, so you can go back later.
rescale.bodyDisk: The server shuts down, changes size and starts again. The disk grows with it and cannot be made smaller again.
rescale.token: Needs a provider token with Read & Write access, under Cloud Providers.
rescale.type: Type the server name to confirm
rescale.failedHint: Check the server at your provider and power it on if it is off.
